clue.text: Man taking in MI5's principal branch

indicators.note: taking in means the name for a man holds the other letters within it

parts.note: Ray is a man's name
MI from MI5, then F, the principal (first) letter of five

explanation.surface: A man recruits the head of Britain's security service as a key branch.
explanation.walkthrough: MI5 is Britain's domestic security service; here it is split, MI kept whole and the 5 spelt out so its first letter, F, can be taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramify is to divide into offshoots, the verb sense of branching out.

clue.text: Having just been shown the pan is excellent

definitions.text: Having just been shown the pan
definitions.meaning: meat only briefly cooked, lightly done
fine or exceptional, as in a fine specimen

explanation.definitionFit: Lightly cooked steak and something unusually fine share this one word.

clue.text: Master of Noise in lodge, maybe?

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
sonic means relating to sound

explanation.surface: The noisiest member of a lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so the adjective describes what goes on in one, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Concerning Tube strike, turn on housekeeper

parts.note: to fist is to strike with the hand
U as in U-turn
a Lar was a Roman household god, guardian of the house

explanation.surface: An Underground strike sparks an attack on the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like London's Underground but means any pipe. 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means pipe-like or hollow, so it concerns a tube.

clue.text: Mafioso, perhaps — one from Italian city entering US state

indicators.note: entering means the reduced city name goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is a short form of California

indicators.note: one from the city means a single I is taken away from its name

parts.note: Rimini is a resort city on Italy's Adriatic coast
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Mafia man, perhaps, arriving in America from an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mafioso is an example of a lawbreaker, hence the 'perhaps' signalling a definition by example.

clue.text: Rogue's accusation: youngster pinched the lot!

parts.note: a rap is a charge, as in beat the rap

indicators.note: pinched means held tight, so the youngster holds the lot inside

parts.note: a scion is a young descendant
all means the lot

explanation.surface: A villain is charged after a young thief stole everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' reads as theft, fitting the rogue, but here means gripped: the youngster holds the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascally scoundrel, an old-fashioned word for a rogue.

clue.text: Drink to town centre's pastoral setting

parts.note: mead is a honey drink

indicators.note: town centre's means the middle letters of the word town

explanation.surface: Toasting the heart of a country town.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy field is a typical rural scene, a pastoral setting.

clue.text: Article about facial hair on a girl

indicators.note: about means the article is turned round

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
tash is short for moustache

explanation.surface: A piece about a girl with a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a girl's name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: D'Arcy, unexpectedly plunging into water, displays stodge

indicators.note: plunging into means the jumbled name dives inside the body of water

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of the name turn up in a surprise order

explanation.surface: Mr D'Arcy's surprise dive into a pond shows his stodginess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' is the anagram signal; the shuffled name plunges into the water, as the surface says, but letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a heavy British teacake of bread dough and lard, a stodgy food.

clue.text: Stand up to kilos, metres etc, interfering with holiday

indicators.note: interfering with means the units barge into the middle of the break

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
kilograms and metres are SI units, the international system

explanation.surface: Someone resents measurement units disrupting their holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand up to someone is to oppose them, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Make a mess of second dish

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: Botching a second course at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To splatter something is to spatter it messily, making a mess of it.

clue.text: 'Down Under': movie with debt to Stallone suggesting trouble ahead

parts.note: Down Under means in Australia, abbreviated to in Aus
pic is a short word for a film
an IOU is a written acknowledgment of a debt
Sylvester Stallone is nicknamed Sly

explanation.surface: An Australian film owing money to Stallone looks like a bad omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in an ill-omened way suggests that trouble lies ahead, an adverbial paraphrase.

clue.text: Bread sandwiching scrap of sea lettuce is bad news for birds

indicators.note: sandwiching means the bread encloses the scrap

parts.note: pitta is a flat bread

indicators.note: a scrap of sea means just its first letter

parts.note: cos is a variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: A seafood sandwich with lettuce harms the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This disease, parrot fever, infects birds, so it is bad news for them.

clue.text: Muscleman of ill repute, sick with love, commits venial sin

parts.note: the word splits as muscle, giving PEC (pectoral), and man of ill repute, giving CAD
ill means sick
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A disreputable bodybuilder, lovesick, commits a minor wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscleman' must be split: 'Muscle' gives PEC and 'man of ill repute' gives CAD. 'commits' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small, forgivable fault, the same idea as a venial sin.

clue.text: Reportedly pedal president's buggy

parts.note: pedal sounds like peddle, and to peddle is to push goods
a chair is the president of a meeting

explanation.surface: The president's bicycle, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' works on 'pedal' only: said aloud it is 'peddle', whose synonym is PUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby buggy is a folding chair on wheels for a toddler.

clue.text: Bog with a flower

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet, as is lav

explanation.surface: A toilet adorned with a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'thing that flows', so molten rock fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock flows from a volcano, so it is a flower in the punning sense of a thing flowing.

clue.text: Plan to go walkabout, corralling sheep

indicators.note: corralling means rounding up and holding, so the wanderer encloses the sheep

parts.note: to stray is to wander off
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A scheme to roam about while herding sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall plan of action, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Rifle fire

definitions.meaning: to rifle a place is to ransack or plunder it
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Both plunder of a captured town and dismissal from work are senses of this word.

clue.text: Ringer with a vision

parts.note: a chimer is one who rings bells

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer with second sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer' hints at a lookalike, but here means a bell-ringer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful imagining, an illusion or vision.

clue.text: Sleazy turn by band necking drinks

indicators.note: necking means swallowing, so the band takes the drinks inside it

parts.note: a stripe is a band of colour
teas are drinks

explanation.surface: A seedy act by a pop group downing their drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip show is a sleazy cabaret act, a turn in the music-hall sense.

clue.text: Mental aberration rendering men incontinent?

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the continent

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: rendering means tearing apart, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lapse that leaves men unable to control themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incontinent' must be read as two words, 'in continent'; 'rendering' (tearing apart) signals the anagram, giving MNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is a disorder of the mind, a mental aberration.

clue.text: Warning: a big picture is being put up

indicators.note: being put up means raised in a down clue, so the picture reads upwards

parts.note: a mural is a large wall painting

explanation.surface: A warning that a large painting is being hung.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarum is an old word for a call to arms, a warning.

clue.text: Frigid artwork — cold composer — hot chow!

parts.note: chill means frigid
an icon is a religious painting
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia

explanation.surface: A list of chilly things ends with a spicy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This spicy meat-and-beans stew is a hot dish, chow being slang for food.

clue.text: Niche curtailed sin

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sloth is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: An alcove that has been cut short sinfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a narrow opening or a place for something, a niche.

clue.text: Swelling menu is a recipe for disaster

indicators.note: a recipe for disaster suggests the letters fall into chaos and are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A chef warns that the menu will end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe' does double duty in the surface phrase but only gives R; 'for disaster' signals the anagram of MENUISA plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term names a bulge in a weakened artery wall, a kind of swelling.

clue.text: Container ship

definitions.meaning: a jug or bowl is a container
a boat or ship is a craft at sea

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a receptacle for liquids and a seagoing craft.

clue.text: Back East German to prepare for fresh conflict first

indicators.note: first means the arming word comes ahead of the German one

parts.note: to rearm is to take up weapons again
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: A German from the East returns to arm for a new war.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearmost part is at the very back, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Stern ruler of 20 gutted by intemperate speech

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: 20 is twenty written out
a rant is wild, angry speech

explanation.surface: A harsh ruler is undone by an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' looks like a cross-reference to 20 down, but it is just the number, spelt out and emptied to TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a harsh, stern ruler who governs cruelly.
